config.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair

personas.name: Ruth
personas.goals: A calm season and a full garden
personas.hidden_agenda: Worried the city won't renew the lease

personas.name: Hector
personas.role: Volunteer who looks after the water system
personas.goals: Fix the leaking main line before summer
personas.hidden_agenda: Has been paying for small parts himself

personas.name: Mina
personas.hidden_agenda: Her friend is next on the waitlist

personas.name: Sam
personas.goals: A fair that pays for the water bill
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to add a food truck the others may not like

agenda.title: Plots and the waitlist
agenda.goal: Reassign abandoned plots and work through the waitlist

agenda.title: Water system and the bill
agenda.goal: Understand the water bill and decide on the spring repairs

agenda.title: Garden rules
agenda.goal: Agree what to do about unattended plots and shared tools

facts.statement: City water rate increase this year = 12%

beats.summary: Abandoned plots and the waitlist; Ruth overstates the waitlist and Mina corrects it gently
The bill is going up; Hector's percentage is off and nobody notices; the main line repair
Vendors, the date, a food truck idea; a detour into the high school's football season
Unattended plots and the shared tools; the lease question hangs in the air

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Now then, let's get started. Plots first. Mina, how does it look?

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: So basically, seven plots were abandoned last season. Nobody touched them after July.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Seven. That's more than usual. And the waitlist must be, what, forty people by now?

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Honestly, it's twenty-nine. It feels like more because people email twice.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Twenty-nine. Still a lot of people waiting.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Do the abandoned plots go straight to the waitlist?

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: That's the rule. First come, first served.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: The thing with those plots is, some of them are a real mess. Bindweed everywhere.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Should we clear them before handing them over?

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: It would be kinder. Nobody wants to start with a jungle.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Totally. Could we do a work day for it?

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: A work day sounds lovely. Maybe the first Saturday in April?

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: I'd come, but my back might not.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: I'll email the next seven people on the waitlist this week and offer them the plots.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Lovely. Will they pay the full fee, joining this late?

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: The fee's forty-five for the year. We've always charged it in full.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Forty-five is pretty cheap honestly, for a whole season.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Then the seven abandoned plots go to the next seven on the waitlist, full fee. That's settled.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Great.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Now then, water. Hector?

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: The thing with water is, it's our biggest cost. Last year the bill was eighteen seventy.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: And it's going up this year?

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: The city put the rate up about twenty percent.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Twenty percent. Goodness.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: So basically, the plot fees don't even cover the water anymore.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: And the main line is leaking near the shed. Every drip is money.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: How much would it cost to fix the leak properly?

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: A plumber quoted me a few hundred. I could do it myself for less, with a helper.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Do we have the money for that?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Super quick, the bank balance is forty-one fifty. So yes, we can cover a repair.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Then let's not wait. It would be good if somebody found Hector a helper.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: My neighbor is a retired plumber, actually. He's very bored.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: A bored plumber is the best kind of plumber.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Mina, could you ask your neighbor if he'd help Hector on the main line?

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Of course. I'll ask him tonight and put him in touch with Hector.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Lovely. Then we fix the main line before the season starts, and the garden pays for parts. Agreed.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: Thank you. I've been buying the washers myself, honestly.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Hector! You should have said.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: It's only a few dollars here and there.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Has anyone looked at whether rain barrels would help with the bill?

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Now then, the fair.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Super quick, so, the fair. It's Saturday, April twenty-sixth.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Lovely. And the vendors?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: We have eighteen vendor slots, and fourteen are already taken.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: That's great for this early.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I also had an idea. What if we had a food truck this year? The taco place on Fifth said they'd come.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: A food truck in a garden?

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Hm. I'd want to think about that. The bake sale has always been the food.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Honestly, people would love tacos. The bake sale sells out by noon anyway.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: They'd pay a vendor fee, too, like everyone else.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Maybe we try it this year and see.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: My grandson's team made the playoffs, by the way. The game's that same weekend.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Oh, congratulations! Is he still playing quarterback?

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: Linebacker now. He likes hitting people more than throwing, apparently.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Now then, we were on the fair.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: So, food truck or no food truck?

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Food truck, this year, as a trial. If the bake sale people are upset, we revisit. Decided.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Totally. I'll confirm with the taco place and send them the vendor form this week.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Do we need more volunteers for the day?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Probably four or five more, for setup and the plant sale table.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: We could really use a sign-up sheet on the shed door.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Last item. The rules. The unattended plots, and the tools.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: So basically, we should say what counts as abandoned. Last year it was a judgment call.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: Six weeks with no watering. That's what most gardens use.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Six weeks feels fair. Should we put it in the rules?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Totally. And send a warning email at four weeks, so it's not a surprise.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Could we vote on it at the spring members' meeting rather than deciding here?

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: That's probably right. It affects everyone.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Sorry, my phone's buzzing, it's my sister. Ignore me.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: The tools. Somebody keeps leaving the good shovel out in the rain.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: It's not me, for the record.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: It's absolutely not me.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: I'm not accusing anybody. I'd just like a hook by the door with a sign.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Hector, would you put up a hook and a sign?

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: Happy to. I'll put up the hook and a sign by the shed door this weekend.

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Lovely. And the lease. The city renewal is due June thirtieth.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: Have we heard anything from the city about it?

turns.speaker: Ruth
turns.text: Now then, I think that's everything for tonight. Thank you, everyone.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Thanks, Ruth.

turns.speaker: Hector
turns.text: Goodnight.
